item.title: Nearly 800 Drones in Two Days: Ukraine's Largest Strikes on Moscow Yet Coincide With New Peace Push
item.body:
## A Sharp Escalation in Long-Range Strikes

Ukraine has carried out what officials describe as one of the largest drone operations of the war against the Moscow region this week, sending waves of unmanned aircraft toward the Russian capital just two days after a similarly massive barrage. Combined, the two salvos are reported to have involved close to 800 drones, marking a significant escalation in the long-range exchange that has increasingly defined the conflict's recent phase.

Russian air defense officials said the majority of the drones were intercepted or jammed before reaching populated areas, though disruptions were reported at some of Moscow's airports, with temporary flight restrictions affecting arrivals and departures. Local authorities in the region reported falling debris in several districts, prompting brief evacuations and inspections, though the overall scale of damage has not been independently verified.

Kyiv has not officially claimed responsibility for the specific strikes, in keeping with its general practice regarding long-range operations deep inside Russian territory. Ukrainian officials have previously said such strikes target military-industrial infrastructure, fuel depots, and logistics hubs that support Russia's war effort.

## Deadly Missile Strike on Kharkiv Region

The drone escalation came in the same week that a Russian missile strike hit a village in Ukraine's Kharkiv region, killing at least ten people, according to regional officials. Ukrainian authorities said the strike hit a residential area, and search-and-rescue operations continued in the hours afterward. The attack drew condemnation from Ukrainian officials, who described it as part of a broader pattern of strikes affecting civilian areas near the front line.

Russian officials have not issued detailed comment on the specific strike, and the circumstances remain part of the broader, contested record of long-range attacks that both sides have carried out against targets they characterize differently — Kyiv typically citing military and infrastructure objectives, Moscow often describing its own campaign as targeting Ukrainian military and energy assets.

## A Parallel Diplomatic Track

Even as the strikes intensified, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine has sent Washington a fresh set of proposals aimed at ending the war. Zelenskyy's government has framed the proposals as an effort to keep diplomatic momentum alive alongside continued military pressure, a dual-track approach Kyiv has pursued at various points throughout the conflict.

According to officials familiar with the discussions, American negotiators are expected to travel to both Kyiv and Moscow in the coming days as part of a renewed push to narrow the gap between the two sides' positions. Details of Ukraine's latest proposals have not been made public, and it remains unclear how closely they align with positions previously floated by Washington or Moscow on issues such as territorial lines, security guarantees, and the timeline for any ceasefire.

## What Comes Next

Analysts note that intensified strikes and active negotiations are not mutually exclusive in this war; both sides have repeatedly sought battlefield leverage even while diplomatic channels remain open. The coming days — with US negotiators reportedly set to shuttle between the two capitals — could offer a clearer signal of whether the current round of talks represents a genuine opening or another interlude in a conflict that has defied quick resolution.

For now, residents on both sides of the front continue to face the immediate consequences of the escalating long-range campaign, even as officials in Kyiv, Moscow, and Washington weigh next steps at the negotiating table.

*This article reflects publicly reported statements from Ukrainian and Russian officials as of this week; details of ongoing military operations and diplomatic talks may evolve rapidly.*
